chapter: Nola band, day job and nightclub work
title: How long the Nola Band lasted and dating by the war
summary: Hard to date; the Nola Band lasted until he quit in 1934; he never went to war.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, you know what about the time when you started in the old band, was that in the twenties? Or earlier? I've been, I was trying to remember that. Was it before the Depression, you think?
I can't, I can't see exactly.
Kind of hard, I tell you. Yeah, it's good.

Forty years, forty years ago, thirty years ago, it was kind of hard to remember. Especially the way this thing used to go, you know, you'd play with this band tonight, tomorrow night, playing some other band, you see.
But the Nola band lasted a pretty good long time.

Oh yeah, it lasted a long time. I think it lasted, I went out of business. All the way until you left? Yeah, quite sure. And I quit in 34, I quit the trumpet playing in 34, in 1934, and I'm quite sure it lasted

until I quit. You might have had a lot of different fellows in that band, they must have switched. Yeah, well yeah, you know, occasionally you change and you get somebody else. But Henry Russ talked to us about the Nola band. Yeah, he played a long time with the band. Do you remember anybody else that played in the band?
No, I can't remember nobody else right now.

You know, something I was thinking about a way to remember things is when the war is over with, you know, when they declared peace, when there's armistice, you might remember that. What were you doing then?

Well, I tell you, I never had to go to the war, so I don't, can't even remember that. I never went to the war, you know. They had some sort of a way to draft them by classes, I don't know, between class B or class A, some kind of way. And then it would be months before they called some of the people in that class, and kept you from remembering anything.
Oh yeah, I just thought maybe you'd remember that.
Yeah, I know, you would try to help me to remember, I know.
